channel.title: CodeScouts Blog
channel.description: Articles on TDD, Clean Code, software architecture and technical coaching for development teams.

item.title: The definitive prompt: turn any AI into a Technical Coach
item.description: A comprehensive, team-tested prompt that transforms GitHub Copilot, Cursor, ChatGPT or Claude into a senior technical coach using CodeScouts' eXtreme Programming methodology. Copy, paste, and your assistant goes from generating code to coaching like a 10+ year senior.
item.dc:creator: CodeScouts

item.title: React Server Components in production: the architecture you need for 2026
item.description: Next.js App Router has transformed how we think about frontend architecture, but Server Components without design introduce invisible coupling. We analyze the mental model, the patterns that scale, and the most common architectural mistakes in production.
item.dc:creator: CodeScouts

item.title: AI coding agents: how to keep Clean Code when AI writes your code
item.description: AI agents generate code at incredible speed, but without disciplines like TDD, Clean Code and refactoring, that code becomes technical debt instantly. We analyze how to integrate GitHub Copilot, Cursor and Claude Code without sacrificing architecture or maintainability.
item.dc:creator: CodeScouts

item.title: GOF Design Patterns

item.title: ID Document - OCR/MRZ Kata
item.description: A mid/advanced kata to practice TDD and optional mocks in a real-world algorithm. The kata consists of implementing an algorithm that converts an ID image into a character string with structured information, then parses that string into an object with the ID data.
item.dc:creator: CodeScouts

item.title: Clean Architecture in Frontend

item.title: Test-Driven Development
item.description: Also known as TDD (test-driven development), it is a programming practice that consists of writing tests first (usually unit tests), then writing the source code that makes the test pass, and finally refactoring the implemented code.

item.title: Types of Tests
item.description: There are many types of testing we can use to confirm that our software continues to work correctly after introducing new changes to the source code.

item.title: GRASP Patterns, the Old SOLID

item.title: Test && Commit || Revert
item.description: Test && Commit || Revert (TCR) workflow - run tests after every production code change. Commit if passing, revert if failing. Learn this TDD-adjacent technique for faster feedback loops.

item.title: 4 Rules of Simple Design
item.description: 4 simple design rules are a set of guidelines that help us write clean, well-designed code. These rules were proposed by Kent Beck, one of the pioneers of Extreme Programming, and are based on the idea that a design is simple when it follows these rules in order of importance.
